headline: Statistical methods for omic data: mediation, network inference, and variable selection
label: Statistical Models For Omics
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply Bayesian, mixed, and knockoff-based models to microbiome, single-cell, and multi-omic datasets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is probabilistic modeling of high-dimensional omic data, where distributional structure or error control is built into inference. Several items use Bayesian formulations: vampW applies a Bayesian Weibull VAMP model to correlated omic features in time-to-event data, BiGER uses Bayesian hierarchical rank aggregation with variational inference for partial gene lists, and JOANA combines continuous Beta mixture scoring with Bayesian networks for multi-omics pathway enrichment. Others model specific data structure directly: ChoruMM hierarchically clusters the genetic relatedness matrix in bacterial GWAS, and a zero-inflated beta mixture estimated by EM handles compositional microbiome mediators. Selection and testing methods, including knockoffs, shadowVIMP, and de-sparsified LASSO for SNP sets, target valid error control. A controlled diagnostic study of GRN inference shows when causal versus correlational methods break under seven pathologies. Common to these is explicit handling of zero inflation, compositionality, and feature correlation.
